reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: The trial shows biomarker evidence of target engagement - exenatide achieved HbA1c reduction (-0.98%), fasting glucose reduction (-1.75 mmol/L), and post-meal glucose improvements. These pharmacodynamic effects confirm GLP-1 receptor engagement and activation of glucose-dependent insulin secretion pathways. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The downstream biology was successfully modulated - glucose homeostasis pathways were activated as evidenced by the glucose and HbA1c improvements with exenatide. The mechanism worked as intended. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite biological activity, the primary endpoint was not met. The difference in HbA1c change between exenatide (-0.98%) and insulin aspart (-0.88%) was only -0.10% (p=0.2534), failing to reach statistical significance. Both treatments were effective, but exenatide was not superior to the active comparator. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: A trend toward more patients achieving HbA1c ≤7% with exenatide (31.7% vs 24.1%, p=0.0779) suggests potential benefit in a subset, but this was not statistically significant. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was an active-controlled trial comparing to insulin aspart, which is an effective diabetes treatment. The trial was adequately powered (n=505) and duration (52 weeks) was appropriate for HbA1c assessment.

failure_modes.evidence: Target engagement confirmed by biomarker changes (HbA1c, glucose improvements) but primary endpoint of superiority to active comparator was not met (p=0.2534)
